title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs-Site Ops, and Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook defines standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation related to SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operations, and the canonical list of top support issues and fixes. The goal is to keep user-facing docs accurate, discoverable, and reliable for internal and external engineers integrating with Redwood Inference.

Audience

- SDK authors and maintainers (internal SDK teams)
- Developer docs writers and technical editors
- Support engineers and Solutions Engineers
- Product and platform engineers who ship API surface changes

Goals and metrics

- Accuracy SLA: All public SDK guides and API examples reviewed at least once every 90 days.
- Critical doc fix SLA: P1 (security or broken example causing outages) fixed within 24 hours.
- Review turnaround: PR reviews for doc changes within 48 hours for normal changes.
- Coverage: Quickstarts covering text-generation, chat, embeddings, and function-calling for each supported SDK (Python, TypeScript, Go)

Document types and when to use them

1. SDK Guides (long-form)
   - Purpose: In-depth usage, architecture, and migration guides for each SDK.
   - When to write: New SDK feature, major API change, or onboarding flows requiring multiple steps.

2. Quickstarts and Templates
   - Purpose: Minimal friction onboarding for new users; copy-paste runnable samples in <5 minutes.
   - When to write: New customers sign-up flows, demo flows, common use-cases (chat, summarization, embeddings).

3. API Examples
   - Purpose: Small, canonical code snippets that map directly to REST/SDK calls. Must be executable.
   - When to write: New endpoints, parameters, or common integration patterns.

4. Docs-Site Operating Procedures
   - Purpose: How the docs site is built, release cadence, CI checks, and ownership.
   - When to write: Onboarding new doc contributors or changing the docs pipeline.

5. Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes
   - Purpose: Curated list of recurring customer problems with root cause and canonical remediation to speed triage.
   - When to write: After repeated support tickets for the same symptom or after a postmortem.

Standards: Writing and formatting

- Use plain, concise language. Prefer active voice and present tense.
- Include TL;DR at the top for long guides (1-2 sentences).
- All code samples must be runnable and pinned to an SDK version (e.g., python-redwood==1.3.2).
- Add a short FAQ section for common follow-ups.
- Include ownership and last-updated metadata in the doc header.

SDK Guide template (required sections)

- Title
- TL;DR (1-2 sentences)
- Audience and prerequisites (SDK versions, account access, API keys)
- Example quick path (1-2 commands + code snippet)
- Detailed walkthrough (subheadings)
- Troubleshooting and common errors
- Migration notes (if applicable)
- Ownership and reviewers

Example SDK guide header table:

| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| SDK | Python (python-redwood) |
| Minimum version | 1.3.2 |
| Owner | eng-developer-experience/SDK team |
| Contact | #devex-docs on Slack, devex@redwood.com |
| Last updated | 2026-12-07 |

Quickstart template (3-step pattern)

1) Install and configure
   - Code: pip/ npm install example and minimal config.
2) Run a minimal request
   - Provide a single, copy-paste runnable example that returns a response in <5s on hosted environment.
3) Next steps and links
   - Link to SDK guide, API reference, and security considerations.

Quickstart example (Python)

1) Install
   - pip install python-redwood==1.3.2

2) Quick request
   - ```python
   from redwood import RedwoodClient
   client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
   resp = client.generate.text(model="rwd-small-1", prompt="Translate to French: Hello world")
   print(resp.text)
   ```

3) Notes
   - Use environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY. For private deployments, set BASE_URL to the private control plane.

API example standards

- Examples must include: language, pinned SDK version, minimal env setup, expected output, and a short explanation of parameters.
- Prefer REST examples where parity exists (curl + JSON) plus SDK equivalent.
- If an example relies on advanced features (streaming, function-calls), include a short diagram and expected event order.

Docs-site operating procedures

- Repository layout: docs/ (content), site/ (static build config), ci/ (lint and tests).
- CI checks on PRs (must pass): spelling check, link-check, code-snippet execution tests (Python/TS), and schema validation for frontmatter.
- Release cadence: weekly content deploy on Tuesdays at 02:00 UTC after CI passes. Emergency docs hotfixes follow the incident playbook.
- Ownership: eng-developer-experience owns the docs site and runbooks; SDK teams own SDK-specific guides and examples.

Doc PR process (step-by-step)

1. Open branch: docs/<ticket>-<short-desc>.
2. Add/update content and frontmatter author/owner fields.
3. Run local checks: make check-docs (runs lint, link-check, exec tests).
4. Open PR targeting docs/main. Add reviewers: owner + devex-editor.
5. Address comments and merge once checks pass.

Review SLAs and cadence

- Minor edits: review within 5 business days.
- Major changes (API surface changes): review within 48 hours.
- Quarterly audit: each doc assigned to an owner for a review every 90 days. Ownership rotations are documented in the weekly doc ops meeting notes.

Top support issues & canonical fixes (current top 8)

1) Symptom: SDK install fails on macOS with pip wheels error
   Root cause: Missing system lib (OpenSSL) or old pip
   Canonical fix: Upgrade pip and install openssl headers: brew install openssl@3 && pip install --upgrade pip && pip install python-redwood==1.3.2
   Owner: eng-developer-experience SDK team

2) Symptom: Streaming responses truncated in Node SDK
   Root cause: Client-side timeout default (10s) too low for certain models
   Canonical fix: Increase request timeout and use streaming client helper: new RedwoodStreamClient({timeout: 60000})
   Owner: SDK team / eng-platform

3) Symptom: Function-calling examples return 500 for private deployments
   Root cause: Private control plane requires additional routing header X-Redwood-Env: private
   Canonical fix: Document required headers and provide programmatic detection snippet.
   Owner: eng-private-deployments

4) Symptom: Embedding mismatch between Python and TypeScript outputs
   Root cause: Different default normalization in SDKs
   Canonical fix: Standardize on L2 normalization in both SDKs; add explicit normalize=true param.
   Owner: SDK maintainers

5) Symptom: Examples referencing deprecated model names fail
   Root cause: Model catalog rename during rollout
   Canonical fix: Always reference model aliases; include migration example using model-version param.
   Owner: model-onboarding team

6) Symptom: Docs-site linkchecker false positives for auth-protected pages
   Root cause: Link checker not using auth token for internal routes
   Canonical fix: Update CI linkchecker to support --auth-token env var and add allowlist.
   Owner: eng-developer-experience Docs platform

7) Symptom: Rate-limited API calls in quickstarts during demos
   Root cause: Using shared demo API key with low quota
   Canonical fix: Use per-demo ephemeral keys or reduce concurrency in examples; add guidance in quickstarts.
   Owner: go-to-market / dev-experience ops

8) Symptom: CI doc-snippet execution failures after runtime bump
   Root cause: New runtime changed default behavior for random seeding
   Canonical fix: Pin runtimes for test execution and set deterministic seeds in examples.
   Owner: eng-infra / docs CI team

How to add a new canonical fix

1. Create a doc under quickstarts-and-templates with title prefix: "canonical-fix-<short-symptom>-YYYY-MM-DD".
2. Add: symptom, reproducible steps, root cause analysis, canonical remediation, owner, and related PRs/CLs.
3. Tag with label: "canonical-fix" and link the doc in this playbook's related_pages.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience (doc ops lead).
- Slack channel: #devex-docs (use for triage, tagging with P0/P1 in subject).
- Pager: For critical production-impacting doc issues (security/credential leaks), follow the incident escalation playbook and notify Security & SRE.
